While the Military said non-inclusion of the rank of Field Marshal in the national warrant of precedence led to confusion and lack of clear orders, top ministry sources made it clear that the matter of attendance at the funeral was left to the judgement of the three Service Chiefs.

The low political and military turnout at Manekshaw's funeral blew up into a major row after objections were raised by both serving and retired defence personnel. While all three Service Chiefs and a Union Cabinet Minister attended Cariappa's cremation in 1993, the senior most political representative at Manekshaw's funeral was Minister of State for Defence M M Pallam Raju and the armed forces were led by Vice-Chief of Army Staff Lt Gen M L Naidu.

While the Army had a valid reason as General Deepak Kapoor was on a tour to Russia, the other two chiefs were present in Delhi. This, insiders say, once again points at the lack of cohesiveness between the forces.

Top government officials confirmed that while Antony was keen on attending the funeral, he was held back due to urgent political commitments in Delhi. But he deputed the Minister of State for Defence for the function.

However, the Navy and the Air Force failed to send any senior officer. Forget the Vice-Chiefs, the two armed forces deputed only two-star level officers from local formations near Wellington to attend the function. This, insiders say, is more of a sore point for the Army than the absence of Antony at the function.

Defence watchers say the entire controversy could have been avoided if set rules were laid and the rank of Field Marshal included in the warrant of precedence. However, the Government's failure to include the rank even after the appointment of three five-star level officers since Independence is being seen as a serious lapse.

The announcement of a state funeral for the top officer was also delayed considerably due to the exclusion from the warrant of precedence. Sources said Antony had to personally call up Prime Minister Manmohan Singh to request for a state funeral for Manekshaw.

While Defence Ministry officials approached the Home Ministry for the state funeral, it is learnt that certain officials initially refused as the rank did not figure in the warrant of precedence. The matter was resolved only after the Defence Secretary cited direct orders from the PMO.

Heading: Nitish bats for development plans of town - Indian Express
Content:
The Bombay High Court rapped the CBI on Monday for the slow pace of its probe into the murder of Jalgaon Congress leader Vishram Patil.

Petitioner Rajni Patil, wife of Vishram Patil, has alleged that President Pratibha Patil's brother, G N Patil, is party to her husband's murder.

"How much more time do you need to complete the investigation?" the court asked before granting the CBI time till July 25 to make headway.

"The case was transferred to the CBI in February last year and there has been no satisfactory investigation so far," the Division Bench of Justice R M S Khanderparkar and Justice P B Majumdar reminded the agency.

Associate Solicitor General Gopal Subramanium, appearing for the CBI, then sought a three-week time although no directions were passed to this effect. Subramaniam informed the court that the agency had already filed a second supplementary chargesheet and that scientific tests like brain mapping, narco-analysis and polygraph tests needed to be conducted on the suspects.

The submission comes even after the court, during the last hearing on June 16, had asked why the CBI had so far not conducted tests on the two suspects, Leeladhar Narkhede and Damodar Lokhande.

The CBI counsel had contended that the agency was awaiting the Supreme Court's verdict on the validity of such tests as investigative tools.

The court then stated, "If the CBI can conduct such tests on the suspects in the Arushi Talwar case, why not in this case?"

Subramaniam submitted that it has been the practice of the CBI to take the consent of the persons concerned before conducting narco tests which they have not received in this case. The court then pointed out two instances in Maharashtra alone in which the CBI has conducted narco tests without the consent of the persons concerned.

Justice Khanderparkar remarked, "Even without narco tests, there is sufficient information on record already for the agency to investigate the role of others."

Rajni's advocate Mahesh Jethmalani argued that the scientific tests are not the last word in the investigations.

Jethmalani asked why the CBI had mentioned only the names of two persons — Raju Mali, who is already dead, and Raju Sonawane — in the supplementary chargesheet.

Jethmalani also said the probe had suffered due to "suppression of evidence" and gave an example of the eye-witness statement, recorded by the CBI on 25 May 2007, of one Rambhau Pawar, in which the latter had given an account of the murder.

Vishram Patil was murdered on February 21, 2005. The court in July 2007 admitted Rajni's petition and began to supervise further investigations of the case by the CBI.

Heading: Dalai Lama envoys in Beijing to begin seventh round of talks - Indian Express
Content:
In his renewed bid to mobilise public representatives, Chief Minister Nitish Kumar on Monday met elected representatives of civic bodies from across the state and asked them to work towards makeover of towns.

The Chief Minister, who has earmarked last Monday of every month for meeting public representatives, heard 84 civic bodies' members including mayors and deputy mayors.

Kumar said the state Government had already started CM civic body development plan under which the main approach road and a park would be developed within limits of every municipal corporation. He reiterated that bureaucrats should listen to public representatives.

Kumar exhorted local bodies' members to set an example by carrying out development work in their respective areas even if it was of symbolic importance. "Let us start a park for our children and the aged. Municipal bodies must use its assets properly and broadbase its tax structure to boost its revenue," Kumar told the public representatives.

The CM said the BPL list for rural areas was ready and for urban areas it would soon be ready.

"As the cut-off point for BPL living in towns is not yet decided by the Centre, there has been a delay in preparing the list," he said.

He said the Centre did not concede the state's demand for increasing kerosene quota by 34 per cent and hence an urban BPL family was getting only 2.5 litre as against 3 litre to a rural BPL family.

Heading: Left parties discuss pullout timing - Indian Express
Content:
The envoys of Tibetan spiritual leader and temporal head Dalai Lama arrived in Beijing on Monday evening to hold the seventh round of talks on the vexed Tibet issue.

"His Holiness the Dalai Lama's special envoy Lodi Gyaltsen Gyari and envoy Kelsand Gyaltsen have gone to China for the formal seventh round of discussions with the representatives of the Chinese leadership," said a statement issued by the office of the Dalai Lama here in McLeodganj.

The Dalai Lama has asked the envoys to make every effort to alleviate the difficult situation of Tibetans in their homeland. He hopes that this round of talks will help resolve the long simmering issue through dialogue in the interest of stability, unity and harmony of all nationality in the People's Republic of China (PRC), the statement said.

The envoys will be accompanied by senior assistants Sonam N Dagpo, Bhuchung K Tsering—both members

of the Tibetan Task Force on Sino-Tibetan Negotiations—and Jigmey Passang from the Secretariat of the Tibetan Task Force, the statement said.

A week ago, a marathon meeting of the task force had been held to formulate the strategy for talks with the leadership of the PRC.

Besides the Dalai Lama and members of the task force, the Prime Minister of the Tibetan Government-in-exile had also attended the meeting.

On May 4, Dalai Lama's envoys and representatives of the Chinese leadership in Shenzhen had agreed to hold the seventh round of the dialogue process, which began in 2002, on a convenient date. The statement signed by secretary to the Dalai Lama Chhime R Chhoekyapa had said "this meeting is taking place at a crucial time".

The discussion will take place on July 1 and 2 in Beijing.

Tracking the Talks

•January 2002: Envoys of Dalai Lama meet Chinese officials outside China in the first face-to-face meeting since August 1993

•May 25 - July 8, 2003: A second round of talks is held between envoys of the Dalai Lama and the Chinese leadership during the Tibetan team's trip to Beijing and parts of Tibet

•September 2004: A third round of talks is held during the Tibetan team's trip to Beijing and parts of Tibet.

•June 30, July 1, 2005: A fourth round of meetings between the Tibetan team and the Chinese leadership is held in Bern, Switzerland. Tibetans say that the trip is designed to "move the ongoing process to a new level of engagement aimed at bringing about substantive negotiations to achieve a mutually acceptable solution to the Tibetan issue".

•February 15 - 23, 2006: Envoys of the Dalai Lama visit China and took part in the fifth round of talks with their Chinese counterparts in Guilin, Guangxi Province of China.

•June 2007: Tibetan envoys meet Chinese authorities for sixth round of talks

Heading: Buddha’s parting shot:  UPA failed on many fronts - Indian Express
Content:
The CPI(M) on Monday said it was discussing the timing of withdrawing support to the UPA, as it felt the Prime Minister was determined to go ahead with the Indo-US nuclear deal. The move comes a day after the CPI(M) formally announced its decision to pull the plug if the Government approaches the IAEA Board of Governors.

CPI(M) sources said Prime Minister Manmohan Singh had earlier said that he would not attend the G-8 summit in Japan on July 7 if there was no consensus on the nuclear deal. "Now it looks like he is going to attend the summit, which clearly shows the Government's intention to go to the Board of Governors of the IAEA to get the India-specific safeguards agreement approved," the sources said.

The CPI and the Forward Bloc are also expected to take decision on the same lines at a meeting to be held here on July 3. The UNPA would also meet on the same day to take their stand on the issue.

The Prime Minister, however, said the nuclear deal was not on the agenda at the Tokyo summit and sought not to attach much importance to the Left threats. "There is nothing new in what the Left parties have said. I have not given up hope still," he said when asked about the CPI(M) Politburo's decision. In all likelihood, any decision to withdraw support to the Government would come after the meetings, sources in the Left said.

While the Congress worked overtime to seek Samajwadi Party's support to bail the Government out of the crisis, the Prime Minister continued his campaign for the deal and made it clear that he was prepared to face Parliament before operationalising the deal. He, however, did not foresee the prospect of early elections despite the Left's obduracy on the deal.

Singh said all that he wanted was that the government should be allowed to complete the negotiation process with the nuclear watchdog and the NSG. "We will grapple with that stage when we come to it," he had said on Sunday when asked about the threat held out by Karat. He said the Government would be able to address concerns of all, including those of the Left parties, on the civil nuclear cooperation agreement with the US. "I hope we can work out...we can still work out an outcome that would satisfy all parties," he said.

"I am not asking for something that the Government should not be doing. I am only saying you allow me to complete the negotiations. There are concerns. I agree to come to Parliament before I proceed to operatioanalise (the deal). What can be more reasonable than this," he had said.

He said the BJP and the Left parties will have an opportunity to discuss the deal in Parliament. "If Parliament feels you (government) have done some wrong, so be it," Singh said.

"All that I want is the authority to proceed with the process of negotiations through all stages like the IAEA and NSG that will not tie down the hands of the country," he added.

He parried a question on the speculation about his attending the G-8 summit in Tokyo saying the nuclear deal was not on the agenda there. He laughed off a suggestion that he would be more comfortable attending the G-8 if the issue was resolved before his departure.

The Prime Minister's fresh bid to push the deal, however, made no difference to the Left stand. "There is nothing new (in the Prime Minister's assurance). We stand by our politburo decision," Karat said.

"This is Government's old stand. We will come back after going to IAEA and NSG, but we say don't go to IAEA. If they do, we will withdraw support," CPI(M) Politburo member Sitaram Yechury said.

He said the Prime Minister has time and again given statements about coming back to the Parliament after completing the processes like signing safeguards agreement with IAEA, getting waiver from NSG and endorsement by the US Congress. "But at that time, it will be more difficult to stop the agreement.

They will say the whole world is in favour of the deal," Yechury said.

Heading: At Bhopal book launch, Advani ‘stays off’ yatra - Indian Express
Content:
West Bengal Chief Minister Buddhadeb Bhattacharjee on Monday said it was not merely the nuclear deal due to which the Left was parting company with the UPA Government, but its overall performance had been dismal.

"If it continues, it will not be good for the people. I am sorry to say that," said Bhattacharjee while speaking at the 80th Annual General meeting of Indian Chamber of Commerce here.

He said there was a chaotic situation in the country with skyrocketing prices of petroleum products and essential commodities. The state Government could not check inflation all by itself as the products had an all-India market.

Bhattacharjee said 16,000 farmer suicides was not a matter of joke. The debt waiver scheme had not done any good to the farmers, only 27 per cent of farmers in the country and 11 per cent in west Bengal take loans from institutionalised credit sources.

Referring to the retail business sector, he said according to the policy of the West Bengal Government, retail chains form multinationals were still not allowed and the state Government did not want any foreign company to open retail outlet in the state.

"In the Left coalition, there are some outfits which are totally against multinationals coming into the retail sector," the CM said, adding there was a gap between the consumer and the market and "we have to modernize our marketing system". "We must go for retail in a big way very cautiously, taking all the stakeholders into confidence," he added.

The CM pointed out that Metro Cash & Carry, a wholesale major from Germany, was also finding some problems in the state.

Pointing out that 2007 drew highest investment to the state, Bhattacharjee advocated treading on the path of industrialisation very cautiously and carefully.

Heading: PM unveils action plan to deal with climate change - Indian Express
Content:
A few hours after criticising the revocation of land allotment to the Amarnath shrine board, BJP's prime ministerial candidate L K Advani chose not to touch the controversy when the stage appeared set for him at the launch of Hindi version of his book My Country My Life here on Monday.

One speaker after another flayed the decision on land revocation, with yoga guru Baba Ramdev even going to the extent of calling the PDP "anti-national", but the Leader of Opposition, who was the last speaker, simply avoided even the mention of Amarnath. As far as book release functions go this must rank as the largest ever with the party and the state Government having pulled no stops to make it successful.

Country's two largest crowd-pulling figures — Baba Ramdev and Sri Sri Ravishankar — flanked Advani on the stage while a large number of Hindu saints sat in the audience. There were figures from other religions too but their number was small.

While talking to reporters a few hours before, Advani had come down heavily on the UPA and accused the Congress of standing by extremists on several occasions. Every one expected him to speak on the raging controversy at the large gathering, which he admitted made him "uncomfortable".

His silence on the Amarnath shrine issue was jarring, especially after the party's announcement that it will become a poll issue. A few minutes before Sushma Swaraj had said that Advani's book predicts events like the Amarnath land transfer.

Instead, the former deputy prime minister sought to reaffirm his loyalty to the RSS. "Whatever I am is because of the RSS," he declared. He took care to mention that RSS leader Mohan Bhagwat attended the launch of the book in March in Delhi and that the Bhopal launch had RSS leader Suresh Soni.

The Bhopal launch was earlier scheduled for June 25, on the 33rd anniversary of the Emergency, so Advani spoke about the black chapter in the Indian democracy. He spoke of Somnath and how Jawaharlal Nehru was willing to reconstruct it, and recalled how Rajiv Gandhi was not in favour of building a temple at Ayodhya.

Just when it appeared that he would launch a broadside on Amarnath he ended the matter calling it "a tale of two temples" and summed up the presence of Baba Ramdev and Sri Sri Ravishankar as "A tale of two sant mahatmas".

Heading: Biman raises protest pitch, says Govt hid N-deal facts - Indian Express
Content:
India on Monday unveiled a national action plan to deal with climate change. Though it doesn't identifying any targets for reducing India's greenhouse gas emissions, it does outline areas where sincere efforts can lead to long-term sustainable development.

Prime Minister Manmohan Singh officially released the action plan that has identified eight 'missions', which will be pursued as key components of India's strategy for ensuring a clean and sustainable development. More and more use of solar energy, ensuring high levels of efficiency in energy use, conservation of water and sustaining the Himalayan eco-system are some of the missions that have been identified under this plan.

Referring to the absence of any commitments to reduce India's greenhouse gas emissions, Prime Minister Manmohan Singh re-emphasised the country's long-held stand that the ultimate objective of the world should be to move towards equitable convergence of per-capita emissions. He also reiterated that India would never allow it per-capita emissions to grow more than that of the developed countries.

"Every citizen of this planet must have an equal share of the planetary atmospheric space. Long-term convergence of per-capita emissions is, therefore, the only equitable basis for a global compact on climate change," Manmohan Singh said after releasing the action plan. "I have already declared, as India's Prime Minister, that despite our developmental imperatives, our per-capita Green House Gas (GHG) emissions will not exceed the per-capita GHG emissions of the developed industrialised countries," he said.

The Prime Minister stressed on the need to tap India's traditional knowledge base to ensure that its developmental needs do not clash with the need to keep the environment clean. "The time has come for us to draw deep from ancient tradition and launch India on a path of ecologically-sustainable development. Our people have a right to economic and social development and to discard the ignominy of widespread poverty. For this, we need rapid economic growth. But I also believe that ecologically-sustainable development need not be in contradiction to achieving our growth objectives," the Prime Minister said.

Heading: Cong could come between SP-JDS merger in Kerala - Indian Express
Content:
In line with the politburo decision taken in Delhi on Sunday, Left Front chairman and CPI(M) state secretary Biman Bose on Monday raised the protest pitch against the Congress and the UPA government. Bose accused the Congress of "suppressing" facts and "misleading" the Left over the Indo-US nuke deal. Vital clauses of the deal were not disclosed to us, including the decision to go to the IAEA, Bose alleged.

The LF chairman also accused the Congress of helping communal forces in the country, besides failing to check price rise and inflation. The Left Front will launch a countrywide campaign against the Congress over these issues, he said.

Bose was speaking at the party headquarters in Alimuddin Street after a crucial Left Front meeting where the situation in Delhi was discussed in detail. "During the UPA-Left meeting in Delhi in October and November last year, the Congress government had said something else on the nuke deal. Now they are saying something else. Last year, they did not tell us that it was mandatory for the Centre to go to IAEA, but now Congress say it's mandatory. This is grossly wrong," Bose said.

Bose said the views that emerged in the meeting has been communicated to their counterparts in Delhi where a final decision will be taken soon. "We are also talking among ourselves. While CPI(M) held talks with CPI on Sunday, the former spoke to Forward Bloc on Monday. Another meeting is scheduled between CPI(M) and RSP on Tuesday. An all-important Left coordination committee meeting is expected to be held in Delhi on July 3 or 4."

The meeting also made clear the Left's strategy of attacking the Congress on communalism and price hike as the n-deal seemingly lacks popular appeal. "There were a number of instances in recent years when communal forces have raised their heads in different parts of the country, be it in Gujarat, Karnataka or Madhya Pradesh. But the Congress did not hit the streets against such forces. Attempts are being made to provide opportunity and undue advantages to communal forces. We will campaign against this," said Bose.

On inflation, Bose said, "The situation has never been so in the past 13 years. The UPA Government has failed to check inflation. Instead, they are pushing for the nuke deal."

Heading: IAF Su-30s to fly in US skies with Korean, French warjets - Indian Express
Content:
The Samajwadi Party's warming towards the Congress on the nuclear issue is set to upset the proposed SP-Janata Dal(S) merger in Kerala. The state unit of JD(S), led by M P Veerendrakumar, Member of Parliament, had announced its merger with the SP, and the JD(S) had begun the spadework to embrace the SP.

However, if the SP led by Mulayam Singh Yadav supports the Congress on the nuclear deal, JD(S), an ally of ruling Left Democratic Front (LDF) in Kerala, would be forced to re-look into the proposed merger.

Many in Kerala unit of the JD(S) feel that merging with SP that props up a Congress Government at the Centre would risk its partnership with CPI(M)-led LDF. "A final decision on the merger would be taken only after July 3, when SP is to make clear its stand on supporting the Congress on the nuclear deal. If SP gives support to Congress, we would have to rethink about the merger," JD(S) state general secretary K Krishnankutty told The Indian Express.

JD(S) all-India general secretary Dr Varghese George said when the merger idea was mooted, the SP had not shown any symptoms of moving towards the Congress. "We approached that party as a non-Congress, non-BJP entity. The outcome of the UNPA meeting slated for July 3 is critical for the merger of JD(S) with SP too," added George.

Merger with another party has become a matter of life for the JD(S) which suffered a spilt when the group led by Veerendrakumar decided to dissociate with former prime minister H D Deve Gowda in 2006. The decision came in the wake of Gowda's decision to form government in Karnataka with the support of the BJP.

Later, JD(S) led by Gowda got the recognition of the Election Commission, forcing other faction, led by Surendra Mohan at the national level, to hug another party.

Heading: Second DU list doesn’t hold out much hope - Indian Express
Content:
India's participation at the Red Flag exercise at Nellis airbase of the US Air Force - seen as a milestone in its military engagement with the US — will be a multi-nation event with elite air units from France and South Korea scheduled to participate in what is often termed as one of the world's toughest aerial combat training exercise.

While IAF will be fielding its frontline Su 30 MKI fighters for the 11-day event — the first appearance of the Russian-origin fighter in North America - France will pose a lofty challenge to them with its latest Rafale multi-role fighters for the exercise.

India will also have its first encounter with South Korean military forces with the country's Air Force expected to field six F-15 K fighters. This would also mark South Korea's first presence at the exercise.

Besides a fleet of six Su 30 MKI aircraft, IAF is expected to send an IL 76 transport aircraft and an IL 78 mid-air refuler to the exercise to be held from August 11-22.

However, enthusiasts, who were looking forward to a contest between the Su 30 MKI and the F 22, may be disappointed, as the USAF has not yet planned to send in its fifth generation fighter for the exercise.

The American force is expected to comprise F-16 and F-15 fighters, electronic warfare aircraft, refulers and C 130 and C 17 transport aircraft.

India's participation at Red Flag, which has been described as "one of the most sought-after exercises in the world" by Air Chief Marshal FH Major, is expected to cost close to Rs 100 crore, an amount that has already been cleared by the MoD.

"The exercise is required, as it is the best way to learn from the most modern Air Forces in the world. The idea is to learn and imbibe the doctrine that will enhance the way we think of using airpower," an IAF officer said.

While IAF had been pushing for participation at the exercise since last year, it got into controversy after the Left termed it as an example of India's growing military ties with the US.

IAF, meanwhile, considers its participation as a great learning opportunity, as the exercise is at present open to only NATO countries or very close US allies.

Heading: Man held with Uzi pistol in Mumbai - Indian Express
Content:
With the second cut-off lists of Delhi University out on Tuesday, many students may hold hopes of making the grade. But here is a reality check: the percentages for most subjects have not gone down more than one to two per cent. This means that all the major colleges still have cut-offs above 90 per cent for its popular courses.

Out of a total 384 seats in SRCC for B Com (Hons), 335 have been filled. Hence in the second list, cut off is being reduced by a mere 0.5 per cent. Earlier it was 94.5-98 per cent. Meanwhile, Hindu is decreasing the cut-off marks for B Com (Hons) by 0.5 per cent and Sri Venkateswara is reducing it by 1.25 per cent.

"Hansraj College only has 100 more seats to fill out of 800. So we are reducing the cut-off for B Com (Hons) and Economics (Hons) by 0.25 and 0.5 per cent, respectively," said Dr S R Arora, Principal.

Girls' colleges are just as competitive. Kanika Khandelwal, PRO of Lady Shri Ram College, says that with more girls getting good marks in the class-XII exams, the competition is really high. "The seats of English and B Com are nearly filled, so we don't have to decrease the cut off much," she says.

Heading: WHO launches new method to detect multidrug-resistant TB - Indian Express
Content:
The Mumbai Police Crime Branch on Sunday evening arrested a man from Mulund (East) and recovered an Uzi submachine pistol from his possession.

"Acting on a tip-off, Unit 5 of the Crime Branch laid a trap and arrested Vijay Manohar Tawde (32) near a bus stop at Jyotiba Phule Road in Mulund (East). He has been remanded to police custody till July 5," said Joint Commissioner of Police (Crime) Rakesh Maria.

"This is a highly sophisticated weapon and one of the most dangerous close combat weapons. The weapon we have recovered is a submachine pistol with a magazine capacity of 32 rounds. In the Indian market such a weapon would cost between Rs 4 lakh to 5 lakh," added Maria.

Police sources revealed that Tawde was also involved in drugs peddling. In 1996, he was arrested by the Directorate of Revenue Intelligence during a seizure of 102 kg of mandrax tablets. He was released in 2006 after serving 10 years of imprisonment.

"Investigations are on to find out how the weapon was smuggled into the city. Tawde has named a few buyers but we can't disclose anything at this stage," said Maria.

In 2002, the Mumbai Police had recovered another Uzi mini-carbine from two members of the Chhota Shakeel gang.

What's a Uzi

A compact, lightweight submachine gun, Uzi was first designed by Major Uziel Gal of the Israeli Defence Forces during the 1948 Arab-Israeli War. The initial model was accepted in 1951 and was first used in a battle in 1956. It was soon developed into a number of better engineered variants.

Heading: ‘Education is the key to make Haryana No. 1’ - Indian Express
Content:
Multidrug-Resistant (MDR) TB cases, which earlier used to take two-three months to be diagnosed, will now take just two days to be detected - thanks to the new techniques launched by the World Health Organisation (WHO) on Monday.

According to experts, MDR-TB is one such form of TB that responds poorly to standard treatment because it is drug-resistant. According to the WHO, about 2 per cent of MDR-TB cases worldwide are being diagnosed and treated appropriately, primarily because of inadequate laboratory services.

The new initiative consists of two projects - the first, made possible through a US$ 26.1 million in funding from UNITAID, will introduce a molecular method to diagnose MDR-TB that until now was used exclusively in research settings. These rapid new molecular tests known as line probe assays, provide the results in less than two days.

Over the next four years lab staff would be trained, lab facilities enhanced and new equipment delivered to 16 countries that would begin using rapid methods to diagnose MDR-TB, including the molecular tests. The countries would receive the test procedures through the Stop TB Partnership's Global Drug Facility, which provides countries with both drugs and diagnostic supplies.

As part of the project, WHO's Global Laboratory Initiative and FIND will help countries prepare for installation and use of the new rapid diagnostic tests, ensuring necessary technical standards for bio-safety and the capacity to accurately perform DNA-based tests. The tests will be introduced in a phased manner from 2009 to 2011 in about 14 countries.

Under a second arrangement, complementary agreement with UNITAID for US$ 33.7 million, the Global Drug Facility will boost the supply of drugs needed to treat MDR-TB in 54 countries, including those receiving the new diagnostic tests. This project is also expected to achieve price reductions of up to 20% for second-line anti-TB drugs by 2010.

All countries receiving this assistance have met WHO's technical standards for managing MDR-TB and already have treatment programmes in place. Some will use grants from the Global Fund against AIDS, Tuberculosis and Malaria to purchase the drugs.

According to estimates made by the International health agency in the global TB report-2008, In India out of the total 20 lakh cases reported, 3 per cent of the total cases develop resistance for the drugs. The prevalence of TB here is 199 cases per lakh population.

Experts in India say the new methods will help save a more of lives. "On most occasions by the time we get the report, the damage is already done. The success rate is very low as the drugs are very toxic. This drug would enhance possibilities of quick diagnosis and early treatment," said RP Vashist, TB programme manager.

Heading: NACIL proposes cost-cutting measures, employees’ union ready to shoot it down - Indian Express
Content:
Haryana is going ahead on a mission to provide the Right to Education to every child, as this is the best way of ensuring rapid and inclusive growth in the long run. Journey from literacy to education is a huge leap forward in the direction of providing equal opportunities to all, so that everyone can participate in today's vibrant economy.

Education for all becomes even more important in the context of modern global knowledge economy. Keeping with the changing trends and needs, Haryana has increased the budgetary allocation for Education Department from Rs 1,600 crore in 2004-05 to Rs 3,200 crore in the current year. We have also declared 2008 as the Year of Education.

Today, education is not only considered a beacon of light to kindle the rays of literacy but is also a key component of planning for development. The state Government is aware that educational opportunities are the tools to bring about socio-economic changes that transform a society into a just and an equitable order. It is by establishing such an order that the noble ideals of our Constitution can be realised and, therefore, to this end my government has been working tirelessly.

The inspiration to promote quality education in Haryana came to me from my grandfather, Chaudhary Matu Ram, who was a crusader in spreading education and abolishing untouchability. He was also the founder president of Jat Educational Society.

Three years ago when we formed Government in Haryana, we focussed on a multi-pronged strategy to ensure that our children get quality education. We took a conscious decision to deviate from the conventional practices and launched reforms in all the three tiers — primary, secondary and higher education. The underlying idea was to lay emphasis on inclusive development in which benefits of education and development would reach all social groups.

To drastically reduce dropout rate of students belonging to weaker sections of society, a comprehensive scheme at the cost of nearly Rs 280 crore was formulated under which all girl students belonging to Scheduled Caste families were given a monthly stipend ranging from Rs 150 to Rs 400. Similarly, boys belonging to these classes were given a monthly stipend ranging from Rs 100 to Rs 300 per month. For meeting all school-related expenses, one-time allowance ranging from Rs 740 to Rs 1,450 was given. Similar benefits for girls belonging to BPL families are being considered.

The results of these efforts are before us as the dropout rate of students belonging to Scheduled Castes and weaker sections has come down significantly. Also, parents who used to withdraw students from schools due to economic reasons are now encouraged to send their wards to schools. These innovative schemes have the potential to go a long way in empowering weaker sections of society.

The state Government has decided to make women the drivers of this collective effort for educational transformation. To ensure that women get higher education, we have set up Bhagat Phool Singh College in Khanpur Kalan in Sonepat district. Sakshar Mahila Samooh scheme has been implemented to ensure participation of educated women in developmental process.

To improve the quality of education in the state, we have enacted a legislation to pave the way for private universities in Haryana. We are also setting up Rajiv Gandhi Education city at Kundli in Sonepat district where 25 per cent seats would be reserved for students from the state. Similarly, we are upgrading Deenbandhu Chhottu Ram Engineering College at Murthal to University of Science and Technology and setting up a medical university at Rohtak. Prime Minister Manmohan Singh has also sanctioned a Central university and an Indian Institute of Management for Haryana.

It is a matter of pride for us that every 10th soldier in the Indian Army is from Haryana. Continuing with this tradition, we are also setting up a defence university.

Haryana has the largest network of EDUSAT (education through satellite) to provide alternative quality input to education for students in schools, colleges and technical institutions. Haryana is the first state to successfully introduce semester system in schools and now, it will be introduced in colleges too.

We have also introduced the concept of teacher's eligibility test in the state on the lines of the one conducted by the UGC. Haryana has one-third of its posts of teachers reserved for women.

To provide livelihood to youth is our avowed mission. The state Government has been expanding its network of technical institutes. We have now 52,000 seats in such institutions from 33,000 three years back. We have resolved to increase this number to 1,00,000 by 2010.

My dream is to make Haryana the number one state in the country through rapid economic growth and by ensuring equal opportunities to all segments of society. Education is the key to achieve this objective. This a daunting task. But all Haryanvis love challenges and so do I.

Heading: Monsoon mayhem on highway of horror - Indian Express
Content:
Alarmed by the financial crisis gripping the National Aviation Company of India Ltd (NACIL), formed after the merger of state-run Air India and Indian Airlines, the Union Government has decided to get more closely involved in the functioning of the ailing firm to help revive it.

As The Indian Express reported over the last two days, NACIL's unaudited losses for 2007-08 have more than tripled to a record Rs 2,144 crore. Its borrowings are close to its limit of Rs 8,550 crore and the company faces a daily deficit of over Rs 8 crore, according to an April-end estimate.

The crisis has been blamed on a range of reasons, including mismanagement, post-merger problems, overspending, an old fleet, overcapacity, undercutting and a complacent workforce, besides rising fuel prices. "The position is grim for the entire industry and more so for the national carrier," said Civil Aviation Secretary Ashok Chawla. "We are going to have intensive reviews of NACIL every month with the first meeting set for Saturday. We will discuss how the financial position is unfolding through fare hikes and cost-cutting measures."

Earlier this year, NACIL had asked the Government for a budgetary support of Rs 1,000 crore, but the proposal is yet to be approved. "Because Air India needs financial assistance, we need to take a clear view in the next two or three months on what should be the quantum of assistance," Chawla said. "We need to decide what is the best manner in which their case can be piloted, whether it should be additional equity or a soft loan or a grant or a mix of all or some of these. We should get a clear idea by the end of September."

Before that, though, NACIL needs to act on a radical cost-cutting wish list prepared at the end of April. The list is spread across rationalisation of routes and operations, aircraft maintenance and repair expenses, fuel management, distribution costs, employee costs and other expenses. For instance, it proposes withdrawal of routes not meeting even the cash costs, phasing out of old aircraft as they consume more fuel and are expensive to maintain, introduction of smaller aircraft on short-haul routes, a 25 per cent cut in sales promotion budget, cuts in wages/variable productivity linked incentives for all categories of staff and even discontinuation catering on flights of less than an hour.

Also, the wish list proposes disposal of surplus movable and immovable assets, deferment of delivery schedule/ sale of delivery slots of new aircraft, stopping dry or wet leasing of aircraft and disposal of old aircraft.

A detailed analysis of estimated savings, if cost-cutting measures are implemented, puts the amount at Rs 947 crore while revenue enhancing measures are projected to yield another Rs 850 crore, injecting a total of Rs 1,797 crore into the sick company this fiscal. Besides listing targets for the management for 2008-09, the document also has a broad vision for the company through 2010-11.

NACIL spokesman Jitender Bhargava said that some of the proposed measures were already being implemented and the Chairman had told all departments of the "difficult time the airline industry, including Air India, is facing and major areas in which savings have to be effected".

However, one indication of how tough it will be for NACIL to return to cruising altitude came earlier this month. The Federation of NACIL Employees, one of the unions, passed a resolution saying it would oppose the 25 per cent wage and benefit cut that was being proposed. "We shall not take this lying down, and shall oppose wage cuts with all the means at our disposal," it said. "The Government and management has in the last four years bled our airlines and crippled it and now wants employees to bear the price of their mistakes."

VISION FOR 2008-09 TO 2010-11

•Formulate risk management policy, including fuel, currency and market risk hedging

•Introduce employee stock options

•Formulate IPO to tap equity

•Appoint independent directors on the board and strengthen the existing board

•Upgrade IT systems and introduce online revenue and expenditure accounting

•Ensure daily profitability

ISSUES CRITICAL TO REVIVE AIR INDIA AND INDIAN AIRLINES

•Yield improvement

•Dispose surplus assets

•Defer delivery schedule of new aircraft

•No more leasing of aircraft

•Dispose old aircraft

•Revenue generation from advertisements

•Review credit facility given to government departments

•Merge offices, counters and manpower at common centres of Indian Airlines and Air India

•Government support in the form of one-time grant towards integration costs of IA and AI

•Equity infusion to increase capital base

•Assistance in the form of soft loan

Heading: Left fails to add reform chapter in state’s education department - Indian Express
Content:
Until the monsoon arrived, this 18.35-km stretch of asphalt was just another arterial link for a city of commuters battling traffic pile-ups to get to work in central and south Mumbai from distant suburban homes. Suddenly, the Eastern Express Highway — used by an estimated 50,000 passenger cars daily — is not a safe route anymore, having accounted for over 200 accidents, minor as well as significant, since June 1. As many as 73 casualties have been recorded on this stretch during the same period — at an inconceivable rate of 3.04 per day.

For motorists, who thought the financial capital's "lifeline" railway that claims an average 10 lives a day is an unsafe bet, driving to work is suddenly a hazardous proposition too.

Linking Sion in central Mumbai to Thane on the fringes of the financial capital and beyond, the Eastern Express Highway is one of the several key roads widened and "improved" under the Mumbai Urban Infrastructure Project, by firms contracted by the Mumbai Metropolitan Region Development Authority (MMRDA). With the MMRDA having spent Rs 125 crore in 2007 on asphalting the Eastern Express Highway and tens of crores in 2008 as well, it's no surprise that the spate of accidents has led to the game of passing the buck.

The traffic police blame the slippery surface, with several officers stating that the surface material — mastic asphalt, used to drain rainwater — is the culprit. "The condition of the highway is such that vehicles are prone to slipping when it rains. However, the MMRDA won't admit this, choosing to shift the blame on rash drivers," said a Traffic police officer.

According to Joint Commissioner of Police (Traffic) Sanjay Barve, lubrication liquid that drips from vehicles mixes with dust on the highway. "During monsoon, when the roads are wet, this lubricant mixes with water, leading to accidents resulting from vehicles slipping," he said, adding, "drivers should take care at such times".

However, the latest accident, on an early Sunday morning, occurred during a long dry spell. As a tempo carrying 20 fishermen skidded, a private bus coming form the opposite direction collided with it, head on. Three fishermen died, nine others were injured in the 20th major accident here in June.

The MMRDA, of course, says the drivers are to blame. "Accidents caused on the highways are due to over-speeding," said Metropolitan Commissioner Ratnakar Gaikwad. "When motorists at high speed apply the brakes suddenly, they are bound to skid on any surface, not just mastic asphalt," he added.

Agrees DCP Shivaji Solunkhe (Traffic): "Even though the streets are wet, it is the responsibility of the driver not to speed beyond the limits. All accidents cannot be blamed on the wet conditions."

Meanwhile, in a complaint filed at the Vikhroli magistrate's court, former MP Kirit Somaiya of the BJP pointed to the worrying number of accidents on the highway, alleging that the cause was faulty construction and improper technology. The magistrate ordered the Vikhroli police to submit a report on July 24.

Mulund-based Abhishek Bondre (26), an employee with a private company at Powai and a regular biker on the Eastern Express Highway, said there was more to the remedy than the asphalt. Apart from lack of policing, he said the streetlights were located at some distance from one another, especially along the Vikhroli portion, "So, there are patches of darkness at night," he said.

Civil engineer and transportation expert Sudhir Badami agreed that blaming asphalt is simplistic: "To give motorists pothole-free roads, the MMRDA used mastic asphalt on the entire stretch," he said, adding that modern cars with better pick-up, plus speeding motorists, were equally to blame.

Gaikwad says the "issue" is being looked into and the MMRDA is installing signage at the chronic accident spots.

But daily motorists along the highway are wondering what else could soon become perilous in Mumbai.

Heading: Diesel scarcity brings Chennai to a halt - Indian Express
Content:
The unrest in Kerala over educational reforms fails to die down. The first month of the current academic year was marred by a raging agitation over controversial portions in the latest textbooks for classes III, V and VII in the state-run schools. The Left Government has been charged with injecting atheism and communism to students.

Religious groups and right-wing political parties have asked the Government to withdraw the textbooks. The agitation, launched by minorities, was taken to streets by the Congress as well as the BJP, leaving a trail of violence across Kerala over the past two weeks.

Over the last one year, education sector in the state has been haunted by controversies over radical reforms suggested by the Left. For the last three decades, education has been a domain of either Kerala Congress or Indian Union Muslim League — both regional parties representing Christians and Muslims, respectively.

In a major shift, CPI(M) took over education and gave the hot potato to party leader M A Baby in 2006 when the Left assumed power in the state. All right thinking people had hailed the CPI(M) decision and expected Baby to streamline the state's education department, which had been in a shambles. But, under Baby, the education department learnt only fresh lessons on mess-up.

First to lock horns with CPI(M) were the Christian organisations over fixing fee for professional courses run by self-financing colleges in the state. The fee suggested by the Government was not acceptable, especially to Catholics who run a chain of professional colleges. The Government moved to seek 50 per cent of seats for general category students in these colleges and that, too, irked the management of these institutions. Catholic Church raised the spectre of revolt, alleging that the Government was attempting to usurp the rights of the minorities. The Government's move to bridle the managements failed after it faced a setback from the judiciary.

The woes of the education department did not end there. Baby planned radical reforms in school sector as well, including intervention of local bodies in the management of aided and government schools. As a majority of local bodies in the state are controlled by the Left coalition, the suggestion was bound to ruffle private managements.

When a government-appointed expert committee suggested that appointments to aided schools, where the Government pays for the staff, should be made through the state Public Service Commission, community organisations again hit the warpath. This time, Nair Service Society, powerful organisation of upper class Hindus in Kerala, joined the agitation. Amid opposition, the Government could not implement several suggestions of the committee.

The move to introduce sex education in higher secondary schools in the last academic year had witnessed protest from various quarters, citing that the programme would lead to moral decadence and sexual anarchy. Consequently, the material for sex education had to be revised. It is, however, not yet introduced in the schools.

The Government's suggestion to do away with separate seating arrangements for boys and girls in schools drew criticism from several Muslim organisations. Religious groups, particularly Christians, were also upset with the implementation of a single window system for admission to higher secondary schools. The move took away the management's right to admit students.

Even this year's results of SSLC exam was caught up in a controversy over record pass percentage of 92.9 per cent. In the previous years, the SSLC pass percentage had never crossed 70 per cent. Baby's detractors alleged that the pass percentage was manipulated to give an impression that LDF's initiatives in the school sector have borne fruits.

The mayhem in the education department would continue if indications were anything to go by and it would be the students from ordinary backgrounds, who depend on the state-run education system, who would be caught in this crossfire between the Government and the agitators.

Heading: DMK-sponsored jallikattu claims youth, 100 hurt - Indian Express
Content:
A severe shortage of diesel has gripped Chennai and its nearby areas for the past two days, affecting mass transport and even the functioning of hospitals.

On Monday, only 30 per cent of the fuel stations in the city supplied diesel, with the others either putting up no-diesel boards or sending off customers at the entrance itself. Those which had stock were crowded by taxis, autos and even swanky sedans that run on diesel. The supply lasted only for a few hours.

This has also affected many hospitals, which depend on diesel generators, thanks to erratic power supply by the Tamil Nadu Electricity Board. As the crisis worsened, diesel was supplied in cans to hospitals after the staff showed ID cards, to prevent diversion of the fuel into the black market.

However, the black market has been thriving for the past few days, selling the Rs 36-per-litre diesel for as high as Rs 80 across the city.

"We are in the dark about the reasons for this shortage. Since Friday, the quantity supplied has reduced by 50 per cent. The impact was relatively less in the past two days as it was a weekend. The situation became serious on Monday when the entire transport facilities ran on full strength," said M Kannan, president, Tamil Nadu Petroleum Dealers Association.

Even if regular supply is maintained on Monday, extra fuel will still be needed to clear the backlog and accommodate panic buying, pointed out dealers who faced the wrath of the public.

"In the case of petrol, the quantity supplied has been reduced by 50 per cent, which spread panic among the public. Hence, when they find a bunk that has fuel stock, they try to fill their tanks and even cans to tide over the 'shortage', which in turn only worsens the situation," said a dealer.

There are also bulk buyers like factories and institutions that take off huge quantities of diesel. "We cannot prevent them from buying in bulk as they are our regular customers and also, there is a lot of money already tied up as credit in the business with them. So if we say no, they will hesitate to make the payments for the stock they have already bought, which will hit us even harder," reasoned a fuel station manager.

Oil companies said that a delay in the import of fuel parcels was affecting the supply, leading to the present shortage, but the situation was expected to improve in the coming days. However, dealers point out that the proposed national strike by lorries and tankers from midnight, Monday, may hamper the movement of fuel, worsening the situation.

Meanwhile, a lorry and tipper lorry owners association has urged the CM to intervene and solve the crisis.

Heading: Come out of ISI shadow: Gogoi to ULFA - Indian Express
Content:
Celebrations to mark Tamil Nadu Chief Minister M Karunanidhi's birthday took a tragic turn with a youth being gored to death, and over a hundred getting injured in the jallikattu sports at Anna stadium.

The jallikattu, which is associated with temple festivals, was being held as a DMK affair. The deceased was identified as Subramanium (25).

The incident occurred on Sunday evening. Transport Minister K N Nehru distributed the prizes to the winners. The event attracted a record number of 1,000 bulls.

The injured were given treatment at a hospital and discharged.

Heading: Dam on Brahmaputra will affect India: former Bangla envoy to US - Indian Express
Content:
A day after an explosion rocked a rural market in Baska district killing seven people, Assam Chief Minister Tarun Gogoi on Monday renewed his diatribe against the outlawed United Liberation Front of Assam (ULFA) and asked its top leaders, including chairman Arabinda Rajkhowa and armed wing chief Paresh Baruah, to come out of the grip of Pakistan's Inter-Services Intelligence (ISI).

"The ULFA is definitely not serving the interests of the Assamese people by taking innocent lives. Rather it is serving the interests of anti-Indian forces including that of Pakistan's ISI. The (ULFA' s) top leaders are having a nice time in Bangladesh under the patronage of anti-Indian forces," Gogoi said in a press conference. He also called upon civil society groups to mount pressure on the outfit to have talks with the Government.

Gogoi, however, said his Government did not recognise the People's Consultative Group (PCG) as a civil society group. "It is a fact that the PCG was nominated by the ULFA, and hence it is not part of the civil society. Being handpicked by the ULFA, it obeys diktats from the outfit and not from the civil society," the Chief Minister said, reiterating his call to PCG members to clarify their stand on the ULFA's demand for 'restoration of sovereignty of Assam'.

Hitting out at the ULFA for causing yet another blast that killed seven and injured over 40 people, Gogoi said the ULFA was definitely on the wrong path and its leaders should accept this.

"I don't know how the ULFA expects to achieve its goal by killing innocent people. There is no question of holding talks with them (ULFA) on demand for sovereignty which is not negotiable," Gogoi said.

Claiming that the ULFA's strength had come down 'drastically' over the years, the Chief Minister said over 13,000 militants have surrendered in Assam since 1991. "The ULFA is now left with only about 1500 cadres, of whom about 300 are at present in Bangladesh and Myanmar," he said.

Meanwhile, the 'A' and 'C' companies of ULFA's 28th battalion comprising about 350 cadres have been disbanded by its armed wing chief Paresh Baruah after they announced a 'ceasefire' last week without any consultation with its top leaders.

Heading: Khandu, Apang get into war of words over Getam abduction - Indian Express
Content:
Former Bangladesh Ambassador to the US Tariq Karim has said that reports of China building a dam on the Brahmaputra would affect India as much as it would affect Bangladesh. He was addressing the strategic dialogue on water and food security during an international conference on 'Responsibility to the Future' in Mumbai on Saturday.

Karim, now a political analyst and a consultant, said only an initiative by India to help emerge a trilateral co-operation among the three nations would help avert an imminent environmental catastrophe. He said the administrative process in India was reactionary, while in China it was anticipatory.

"China has 22 per cent of the world population and has access to 8 per cent of fresh water. It is anticipating a water crisis. Building a dam on Brahmaputra would address its water and energy issues. However this would result in 60 per cent less water to India," said Karim.

He said when he was the Ambassador posted at Beijing he mooted the idea of cooperation between India, China and Bangladesh. "China was not receptive, while India said such cooperation was not possible. It was an idea whose time had not come. Now, I think the time has come," said Karim.

Why would China oblige India? "The answer is global warming and climate change. Himalayan glaciers are melting, Gangotri has shrunk, in 40-50 years the rivers originating from the glaciers would become seasonal putting China's ambition of constructing a dam on the river in jeopardy," said Karim.

According to Karim, the key to the existence of the Himalayan glaciers lies in the ecological balance in regions of India and Bangladesh. He emphasised that in the times of global warming and climate change no nation can survive in isolation as environmental degradation in one region would affect its neighbouring regions. "India has to address China's concern and only then will the bigger nation lend its ear," said Karim.

He said the situation was similar to the one that existed during the signing of the Ganges treaty, between India and Bangladesh. "In the treaty Bangladesh was not in a position to coerce India which had an upper hand being a bigger nation. Bangladesh got India's attention when it addressed India's concerns."

Heading: Vision 2020 to bring region and rest of India closer - Indian Express
Content:
A day after former chief minister Gegong Apang refuted Arunachal Pradesh Chief Minister Dorjee Khandu's contention that one of his son's abductors was a relative and blamed the state Government for shielding the accused, the CM on Monday hit back at his immediate predecessor for making "highly reactionary and inappropriate" statements against the Government.

The state Government had claimed that Tahak Tatak, who was arrested along with two others on June 21, was Getam's maternal uncle.

"It is extremely unfortunate that a person of Gegong Apang's stature, who has been the chief minister of this state for 23 years, has issued such a reactionary and inappropriate press statement in an effort to further politicise the kidnapping of his son Getam Apang and his friend Narendra Rai. The Government has taken strong objection to the statement, which in its view is ill-informed and without any basis," Khandu said in a statement issued at Itanagar.

"Tatak is neither our relative nor in any way associated with our family. It is the chief minister (Khandu) who was trying to project him as our relative. In fact, Tahak Tatak is a policeman with a criminal background who was dismissed from service after he was involved in a motorcycle theft case," Gegong Apang had said.

Apang had also hit out at Khandu and said it was unfortunate that a person holding a "responsible post" like a chief minister's was making a statement without any basis.

Heading: Meghalaya launches EDUSAT - Indian Express
Content:
Prime Minister Manmohan Singh will release the Vision 2020 document for the North Eastern Region (NER) on July 2. Aimed at bridging the yawning gap between NER and the rest of the country, Vision 2020 has already been adopted by all eight states in the region, said the Ministry of Development of North Eastern Region (DoNER) and the North East Council.

The document estimates that in the next 12 years, investments worth Rs 13 lakh are needed here to help NER catch up with the rest of the country.

The NER Vision 2020 essentially envisages the adoption of a multi-pronged strategy to ensure "inclusive development in the region". Key components of the strategy include empowerment of people by maximising self-governance and participatory development through grassroots planning. It also stresses on rural development with a focus on improving agricultural productivity and creation of non-farm avocations and employment.

Vision 2020 suggests a focus on augmenting infrastructure, including rail, road, inland water and air transportation to facilitate a two-way movement of people and goods within the region and outside.

It also underlines the importance of promoting agro-processing industries, modernisation and development of sericulture, investment in manufacturing units based on the resources available in the region, harnessing the large hydroelectric power generation potential and focus on developing tourism.

Heading: Blast at Diphu, none injured - Indian Express
Content:
Meghalaya became the second state after Tripura in the Northeast to launch EDUSAT, a satellite-based education project. Meghalaya Education Minister Manas Choudhuri on Monday inaugurated EDUSAT, which would help provide distant education to students living in remote and inaccessible areas. The first EDUSAT in the country was launched in Karnataka in March 2005.

The Shillong based North East Space Application Centre (NESAC) co-ordinated by Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) helped the state to launch the satellite education project.

The satellite education will enable teaching and learning at various levels in the 50 Satellite Interactive Terminals set up in remote areas of the state. The project will use satellite and videoconferencing for the purpose. A hub and a studio will be set up in

Shillong with Satellite Interactive Terminals (SITs) in different schools including those in rural areas which would be linked to the hub.

Launching the project, Chaudhuri said this would act as an instrument of social change by altering human perspective and transforming the traditional mindset of teachers and the students.

Heading: Anxious for an heir, this couple defy age to have a male child - Indian Express
Content:
A bomb, planted by the ULFA, exploded near the deputy commissioner's office here on Monday. However, no casualty was reported. The time-device planted by the ULFA's 27 battalion exploded near the deputy commissioner's office and the district agriculture office in the heart of the town at 1.25 pm, the police said. There was no casualty as no one was present on the spot at the time of the explosion.

A search operation has been launched to nab the ultras who had planted the bomb, the police said.

The ULFA's 27 battalion is active in the hill district of Karbi Anglong of which Diphu is the headquarter.

Heading: New timings from today, 242 trains to get faster - Indian Express
Content:
Charan Singh, 76, hobbles to the juice shop to get fresh pomegranate juice for his wife Om Kali, who is in her late 60s and recuperating in a Muzaffarnagar hospital after she delivered twins six days ago.

They wanted a son, and it was this wish which drove them to push all boundaries. "How could I die without a son and leave all my property to others? My brothers are trying to take over my property. My daughter is taunted by her in-laws for not having a brother. I could not bear it any longer," a visibly agitated Singh said.

The twins — a boy and a girl —are both in critical condition. Both weigh a little over 1 kg and are kept in an incubator at Jaswant Singh Hospital in Meerut. The couple had three daughters, one died a few years ago. One of their daughters is married and has four children, the eldest being 16 years old. The third daughter is 22 years old.

Having retired as a supervisor in the Agriculture Department in Meerut, Singh began his research several years ago. "I am a poor man, but for a son I was ready to invest as much as I could," he said. So he took a loan on his agricultural land to get all possible treatment and met several doctors.

Two years ago at his village — Dhogat — close to Bhagpat, a retired Army jawan Jaibeer and his wife underwent IVF treatment. Jaibeer's wife was in her late 40s, but the couple managed to have a son.

Impressed, Singh decided to begin afresh his quest for a son. Now, being blessed with a son is nothing short of a life-time achievement for him and he happily shares his story with anyone who is interested in hearing about it. "I just hope my children survive," he said.

Om Kali, however, is irritated by relatives and friends who ask intrusive questions.

"When she was brought to us on June 24, she had internal bleeding, which was dangerous for the mother and the twins. We carried out a C-section on her immediately," said Dr Nikhat Fatima at Ganga Ram Hospital where Kali is still admitted.

For the happy couple, hope was born in the clinic of Dr Sashee Singh and Dr Anirudh Singh in Meerut. Dr Singh and his wife have been running the clinic in Mawana for the past 20 years. Since 2005, they have been offering IVF and other fertility-related treatments.

At their clinic in Meerut, a smiling picture of the doctor couple holding their first IVF baby welcomes hopefuls. The first IVF baby was born on December 10, 2005 to Akhilesh Rastogi, a document writer, and his wife Seema. "We give IVF treatment to at least 200 couples every year. The success rate is 35 per cent," Dr Anirudh Singh said.

To save themselves from legal hassles, the doctor couple have put down Om Kali's age as 45 years in their record. "We were told that she is in her late 60s, and I am sure she is that old. But to ensure there are no problems, we have recorded her age as 45," Dr Anirudh added.

For this doctor couple too, birth of the twins is a landmark in their career.

"Her menstruation period had stopped more than a decade ago. It was definitely a huge challenge," Dr Singh added. The doctor couple have still not seen the twins, as they flew off to America a month before the delivery and just landed two days ago.

Heading: Chhattisgarh begins distribution of land titles to forest dwellers - Indian Express
Content:
The Indian Railways will come out with a new railway time-table on July 1, as part of its annual exercise of revising the time-table to cut down travel time and increase speed of trains. Under this, 242 Mail/Express trains would be speeded up while three pairs of trains will be converted to Superfast services.

The 242 Mail/Express trains to run faster include nine Rajdhani Express, four Shatabdi Express and 1 Garib Rath Express services. The journey time of these trains would be reduced by 5 minutes to 45 minutes, said railway officials. Railways are publishing one million copies of this new time-table.

The three trains being upgraded to Superfast services are Yesvantpur-Korba Express, Pune-Darbhanga Express and Sonpur-Jammu Tawi Mourdhwaj Express. Significantly, the number of trains being converted to Superfast this year is far lower compared to previous years. Since Superfast trains have an additional "Superfast Charge" in ticket prices, the move has often drawn more flak than credit for the ministry.

Among the Rajdhanis, the New Delhi-Bhubaneswar Rajdhani will reach its destination 45 minutes early while the Sealdah-New Delhi Rajdhani will reach 25 minutes early and the Kolkata-New Delhi Rajdhani will be speeded up by 20 minutes.

Heading: Good news from Met: monsoon will be normal - Indian Express
Content:
The Chhattisgarh Government has set in motion a process for distribution of land ownership deeds to 4.5 lakh families of forest dwellers so that it can be completed before the upcoming assembly elections in the state.

Land for the beneficiaries is to be distributed under the Scheduled Tribes and Other Forest Dwellers (Forest Rights) Act 2006 and its rule framed in 2008, which also covers those who now reside outside the forests but are in possession of forest land.

A high-level meeting, which reviewed the progress of implementation of the scheme, directed the district administration to expedite the processing of claims submitted by the forest dwellers, an official spokesperson said. While 4.5 lakh families are to be benefited under the scheme for distribution of 'pattas', 2.5 lakh claims have reached the sub-divisional level committees so far. State, district and sub-divisional level committees have been constituted, while forest rights committees have been set up in 14,864 villages, after organising gram sabhas.

The spokesperson clarified that inclusion of those now residing outside the forests under the scheme was on the basis of the decision of the Centre.

Meanwhile, Chief Minister Raman Singh announced during the last leg of his 'Vikas Yatra, that his Government was formulating a Rs 71-crore scheme to develop forest villages in the most remote areas of the state. "The funds will be utilised to make basic facilities available in these remote villages," he added.

Pointing out that his Government has taken a series of steps to protect the rights and welfare of forest dwellers, he said Rs 150 crore has been disbursed as bonus to tribal forest dwellers engaged in the plucking of tendu (Beedi) leaves from the forests.

After coming to power in 2003, the BJP had also withdrawn more than 2.25 lakh cases registered over the years against forest dwellers, under the Forest Conservation Act.

Heading: Police say arrest of Nazi official in Goa could be media hoax - Indian Express
Content:
In these times of rising prices and skyrocketing interest rates, the only good news seems to be coming from the Met department which confirmed its earlier forecast of a near normal monsoon rainfall this season.

The Indian Meteorological Department (IMD) on Monday said rainfall for the whole country in the June-September season was likely to be 100 per cent of the Long Period Average (LPA). This is one percentage point more than what it had predicted at the start of the season in May.

The likelihood of normal rainfall is good news for the Indian economy which has been reeling from record inflation for the past few months. Normal rainfall is extremely vital for the agriculture sector, which provides livelihood to a majority of Indians.

IMD said two of the four broad geographical regions were likely to get excess rainfall this season. Both North-East and Central India were expected to get 101 per cent of the LPA. North-West India, on the other hand, was likely to receive 96 per cent while the southern peninsula could expect 98 per cent.

The early arrival of monsoon in Delhi and northern areas of the country was not likely to make much difference to the overall rainfall in the country but it had certainly resulted in an extremely wet June. The accumulated seasonal rainfall over the country as a whole during June 1 to 29 was 121 per cent of its LPA.

July was expected to be slightly drier, IMD said, predicting 98 per cent of LPA rainfall in the month.

This year's monsoon had arrived on the Kerala coast on May 31, a day before its scheduled date of June 1. Thereafter, it progressed rapidly northwards, reaching Konkan and Goa by June 7. The rapid progress continued with monsoon reaching Gujarat, Vidarbha, Chhattisgarh and Jharkhand by June 12. By June 15, it had arrived in Delhi, two weeks earlier than normal.

Though happy with the progress, the Met department had refused to read too much into the early arrival, saying it would not have much bearing on the overall rainfall during the four-month season. The latest forecast seems to confirm that trend.

Heading: Jharkhand landmine blast kills senior cop - Indian Express
Content:
Reports on the arrest of an alleged Nazi war criminal on the Karnataka-Goa border on Friday could be a media hoax, one that even took local intelligence officials for a ride.

A prominent Goan blog, that has in the past highlighted shortcomings of the Indian media, on Monday put up a post saying it was set to reveal 'Nazi-Gate: How the media turns a legendary German composer into a Jew-slaying Nazi varmint'.

The blog has put out a teaser stating 'the truth behind Perus Narkp' would unveil one of the most telling stories about the media in India, especially in Goa.

Reports had emerged from Hubli and Belgaum in Karnataka and from Goa over the weekend that quoted an e-mail press release from a unit called Perus Narkp announcing the arrest of an 88-year-old man, Johann Bach, who was a former colonel in the Nazi Waffen SS and was hiding in Goa.

Perus Narkp was identified as the intelligence wing of the Berlin-based German Chancellor's Corp and Johann Bach — a namesake of the famous composer — was even identified as a brilliant pianist himself.

After reports of the arrest emerged first in Goa and at Hubli and Belgaum, field officers of the Karnataka state intelligence sent a report to the intelligence headquarters in Bangalore conveying media reports of the arrest of a Nazi war criminal.

Karnataka Additional Director General of Police (intelligence bureau) Shankar Bidari when contacted said his office had received an oral field report about the arrest but added that state intelligence and police officials were not involved.

The Karnataka intelligence official also said the arrested Nazi war criminal had been deported to Berlin. Israeli groups hunting for war criminals around the world had traced Bach, he added.

"However, it was an oral report that we received. The case did not happen within Karnataka's jurisdiction, so we did not follow it. Lots of things happen on the Internet and we cannot authenticate everything," Bidari said.

"We have only been reading about this in media reports. We are not wasting our time over it," Karnataka Director General of Police R Srikumar said on Monday.

Police officials in Hubli and Belgaum have over the last three days maintained they had no knowledge of the arrest. "The local police in Belgaum are not aware of any arrest if it was indeed carried out. We have no knowledge," Belgaum Inspector General of Police Raghavendra Auradkar said.

Karnataka Home Minister V S Acharya also denied any official information on the arrest and maintained it was restricted to the media. The Germany embassy in New Delhi and the consulate in Mumbai also said they had received no information of the arrest. Embassy officials said they could not confirm the existence of a German intelligence wing called Perus Narkp.

Journalists from the German publication Der Spiegel who contacted The Indian Express said there is no existence of any war criminal named Johann Bach in their exhaustive lists.

Heading: Naxal attack: bulky rucksacks stood in way of jawans’ rescue - Indian Express
Content:
Five policemen, including a DSP, his bodyguard and driver were killed in a landmine blast at Pundgiri village, 4 km from Tamar police station in Ranchi district, on Monday evening.

A senior police officer said after patrolling near Lungtu hill, a team comprising CRPF and Jharkhand police led by DSP Pramod Kumar was returning to Tamar police station by their van. "As soon as their vehicle approached the culvert, a landmine exploded. The impact of the explosion was so much that the vehicle went up in the air like a football and when it fell on the surface, it was completely smashed," DIG R K Mallick said.

Three victims — Kumar, 28, an officer of the Jharkhand Police Service, his driver Kanahi Singh and bodyguard P Lakra — died on the spot. Two constables of the state police — Kosmos Toppo and Arun Singh — succumbed to injuries on the way to the Apollo hospital. Two other injured constables of the Jharkhand Armed Police were hospitalised. "Their condition is critical," said a staffer of Apollo.

Raghuvar Munda, a 45-year-old resident of Tamar, said after the explosion, the Naxalites opened fire on the policemen. "But the firing stopped after more cops arrived," he added.

The incident, suspected to be the handiwork of the CPI(Maoist), has demoralised the police. "Despite our best efforts, the helicopter was not made available.This delayed the rescue work and by the time we picked up the bodies and rushed to Apollo, it was too late," said a junior officer.

Heading: Salwa Judum leader among 3 killed in Bastar - Indian Express
Content:
Bulky survival packs which normally save their lives while fighting Maoists deep inside the jungles may have turned into deathtraps for the jawans of the Andhra Pradesh Greyhounds after they were ambushed by Maoists while crossing a reservoir on the Orissa-Andhra border on Sunday.

Hopes of survivors began fading on Monday evening after seven of the 39 jawans who went missing on Sunday were found, and the body of constable Uday Nath from Warangal district was recovered from the forests by search parties. However, the fact that no more bodies have been recovered so far from the reservoir and the forest has kept alive the hopes of the police and the families of the missing men. Navy divers and choppers are still searching the area.

Sources in the Greyhounds, an elite anti-Naxalite unit of the Andhra Pradesh police, said they fear that the missing jawans drowned because they were probably unable to take off their rucksacks, each weighing 10-11 kg, in time to swim to the surface after the attack overturned their boat.

"When the jawans came under fire they took positions in the boat and in doing so the boat turned turtle and many jawans went under the boat. It would have been difficult to get the heavy rucksacks off as they were trapped under the boat and probably could not swim to safety," an officer said.

Twenty-three jawans, who did away with the rucksacks, swam ashore. There is disbelief and anger within Andhra Pradesh police over the manner in which the Greyhounds jawans became sitting ducks for a Maoist attack. The Greyhound top brass is unable to explain the wisdom behind 55 jawans, five other police personnel and two boat operators, getting into a single boat to cross a reservoir in the heart of Maoist territory surrounded by thick forests where an ambush is very likely.

"To save time, the jawans were crossing the reservoir in a boat. The Maoists knew about the police movement on the reservoir. They set up an ambush from atop a hillock and used so much firepower that it is unbelievable," said an officer with the Greyhounds. It is believed that over 100 Maoists fired from the hilltop using automatic weapons and light machine guns.

DGP S S P Yadav said seven of the 32 jawans who were reported missing on Sunday after the incident were found by a search party early Monday morning. "Twenty-three jawans swam ashore after the incident on Sunday while the rest were declared missing. Of these, seven were found walking in the forests nearby by our search parties. Not a single body has been found yet, neither in the reservoir nor in the surrounding areas. So we are hopeful they are safe somewhere. Half a dozen helicopters are scanning the surrounding forests and Navy divers are also searching the reservoir," Yadav said.

Police officials said the ambush on the Greyhounds was probably carried out by the Maoist Military Committee of Andhra-Orissa Border Special Zonal Committee. It was set up by the Maoists a fortnight ago to resume attacks on the Andhra-Orissa border. Anti-Naxal units of both states had launched search-and-combing operations after an intelligence tip-off that training camps were being held in the area.

Heading: Council works on India’s future educational needs - Indian Express
Content:
